content.fact: Cross-project references in dbt use `{{{{{{{{ ref() }}}}}` to enable multi-project deployments on Enterprise plans.
content.quote: `{{{{{{{{ ref() }}}}}`s now work across dbt projects on Enterprise and Enterprise+ plans.

content.fact: dbt’s governance features allow role-based access control across multiple projects, enhancing security and compliance.
content.quote: dbt's governance features allow you to manage access to your dbt models both within and across projects.

content.fact: Groups in dbt organize nodes in the DAG for model access management, allowing assignment of ownership.
content.quote: With groups, you can organize nodes in your dbt DAG that share a logical connection and assign an owner to the entire group.

content.fact: Model versioning in dbt helps manage model evolution and enables teams to adopt changes gracefully without breaking downstream dependencies.
content.quote: when coordinating across projects and teams, we recommend treating your data models as stable APIs. Model versioning is the mechanism to allow graceful adoption and deprecation of models as they evolve.

content.fact: Access configurations in dbt allow precise control over who can reference specific models, facilitating secure collaboration.
content.quote: access configs allow you to control who can reference models.

content.fact: Staging environments resolve cross-project references to Staging data, ensuring isolation from Production environments.
content.quote: cross-project references from development and 'Staging' environments will resolve to 'Staging,' whereas only references coming from 'Production' environments will resolve to 'Production.'
content.supports_objective: Understanding how environment types relate to cross-project references

content.fact: Model contracts enforce data structure standards in dbt models, causing builds to fail if contracts are not met.
content.quote: Should a model fail to adhere to its established contracts, it will not build successfully.

content.fact: Models in dbt can have access modifiers: Private, Protected, or Public, controlling their referenceability across projects.
content.quote: A model access modifier in dbt determines if a model is accessible as an input to other dbt models and projects.

content.fact: Cross-project references cannot use duplicate project names as each must be unique in your dbt account for proper resolution.
content.quote: Cross-project references require that each project 'name' be unique in your dbt account.
content.supports_objective: Understanding how environment types relate to cross-project references

content.fact: Model versions allow testing of changes in downstream systems, useful for managing impacts on existing contracts or dependencies.
content.quote: Creating a new version of the model is useful to signify this change.

content.fact: If a model changes access from Public to Protected, it is considered a breaking change impacting downstream consumers.
content.quote: This would be a breaking change for downstream consumers of that model.

content.fact: Deploy jobs can be triggered by a set schedule using intervals, specific hours, or cron schedules. For scheduling, `Intervals` allow jobs to run every specified number of hours; `Specific hours` require entering hours in UTC.
content.quote: You can create a deploy job and configure it to run on scheduled days and times. Use this option to set how often your job runs, in hours.
content.supports_objective: Scheduling a job to run on schedule

content.fact: A deploy job's commands can be customized to include multiple dbt commands, with the default being `dbt build`.
content.quote: By default, it includes the `dbt build` command. Click **Add command** to add more commands

content.fact: Using environment variables allows customization of project behavior when a deploy job runs.
content.quote: Define environment variables to customize the behavior of your project when the deploy job runs
content.supports_objective: Configuring optional settings such as environment variable overrides, threads, deferral, target name, and dbt version override

content.fact: The `Run when another job finishes` feature requires the dbt account to be on Starter or Enterprise-tier plan to configure job chaining.
content.quote: your dbt account must be on the Starter or an Enterprise-tier plan
content.supports_objective: Configuring jobs to be triggered after other dbt jobs (job chaining)
